```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(gatekeepR)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Thresholds are estimates with evidence and status, not magic constants. List
the available methods with:

```{r methods}
gk_threshold_methods()
```

Each marker names its method in the panel (`threshold_method` and
`threshold_args` in `gk_panel()`), so a batch run and the review application
estimate the same thing. `gk_thresholds()` then returns one row per image and
marker. A method may return an explicit not-callable status instead of a cut;
inspect the status before treating a marker as usable.

```{r threshold-run}
cfg <- gk_example_config()
prep <- gk_prepare(gk_simulate(n_cells = 300L, seed = 7L), cfg, quiet = TRUE)
thresholds <- gk_thresholds(prep, cfg, seed = 7L)
as.data.frame(thresholds)[, c("marker", "method", "status", "estimate")]
```

The same table can be drawn. Markers without an estimate keep their row and
state why they have no cut; the density view shows the evidence behind one
estimate.

```{r threshold-plots, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE), fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, fig.alt = c("Dot chart of the threshold estimate of each marker on one simulated image, coloured by status; markers that are not callable show their status as text instead of a point.", "Density curves of the CD3e score for all cells, the negative pool and the positive pool, with a dashed vertical line at the estimated threshold between the two modes.")}
image_id <- prep$cells$image_id[[1L]]
gk_plot_thresholds(thresholds, image_id = image_id)
gk_plot_density(thresholds, marker = "CD3e", image_id = image_id)
```

## Clipped scores and the mixture method

`gk_correct(method = "robust_z")` clips scores to the range from -5 to 5. A
strongly stained marker then has many cells tied at 5. A Gaussian component
cannot describe such a point mass: the fit would shrink onto the tied values
and place the cut next to the bound, so that clearly positive cells below the
bound are called negative. The `mixture` method therefore returns
`NOT_CALLABLE_NO_SEPARATION` when at least nine in ten cells of a pool are
tied at the bound of the score range. Use the `valley` or `tail` method for such a marker,
or estimate on uncorrected scores.

Manual corrections can replace an estimate through the review ledger. The
original estimate remains in the ledger, allowing the final result to explain
which cut was used and why.
